subject: Post-call: Embeddings integration & auth/routing checklist
messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
To: Sam Torres <sam.torres@finline.io>, Priya Narang <priya@finline.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: Embeddings integration & auth/routing checklist

Hi Sam / Priya —

Great to meet you both on the call this morning. Quick written recap + next steps so your engineers have a single reference. Please flag anything I missed.

High-level goal
- Replace current vector store (Pinecone) for document search with Redwood embeddings + in-house reranker for prioritized results. Need a migration path that preserves doc IDs and relevance tuning.

Action items (we can split between infra and app teams)
1) Auth & networking
   - Decide whether you'll use a single Redwood API key per service account or short-lived keys per host. We recommend starting with API keys and a rotating schedule (we'll share guidance). If you want VPC/private deployment later, we can map to service accounts.
2) SDK + routing
   - Use Redwood's embeddings batch API for bulk import and the streaming SDK for on-the-fly indexing. We’ll provide language SDK examples for Node/Python.
3) Embedding dimensions & normalization
   - Recommended starting dimension: 1536 for our base semantic models (we can validate sample vectors). Normalize vectors with L2 before indexing; keep consistent tokenization and lowercasing rules.
4) Batching and throughput
   - Start with batch_size=128 for initial imports, adjust based on memory and throughput. For ongoing ingestion, prefer small batches (16–64) to keep latency predictable.
5) Migration from Pinecone
   - Export vectors + metadata from Pinecone snapshot. Maintain external_id mapping so doc_id -> vector_id is preserved. We suggest a two-step migration: dry-run index in parallel, then cutover once consistency checks pass.
6) Reranker / scoring
   - We'll give you an example reranker flow: candidate generation via ANN search -> reranker model for relevance -> final scoring. Keep the original Pinecone-relevance score as a field during comparison.

Questions for your engineers
- Rough estimate for total documents to migrate (count + avg tokens per doc)?
- Are you currently normalizing vectors on export or relying on Pinecone settings?
- Do you have an internal job scheduler (Airflow / Prefect) to orchestrate bulk imports?

Attachments included: migration plan draft + API key rotation doc.

Next steps
- Sam: can you share your engineering contact and an export sample by Monday so we can validate vector dims and sample quality?
- We’ll schedule a short runbook walkthrough (30 min) next week to walk through the SDK snippet and the cutover checklist.

Thanks —
Ava Chen
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-call: Embeddings integration & auth/routing checklist

Thanks Ava — good summary. A couple quick clarifications from our side before we share an export: 

1) Vector dim: current Pinecone index is 1536 but we're also experimenting with 768 from a different model for cost reasons. If you recommend 1536 for parity, is there a straightforward mapping/upgrade path from 768 to 1536 (or would that require re-embedding)?

2) Batching: our infra team favors larger batches for faster bulk import, but we are constrained by a single 16GB GPU during warm windows. Any specific batch_size ceiling you recommend for a single GPU import job?

3) Auth/rotation: we currently issue long-lived keys for one ingestion service. We can rotate but would like a recommended rotation frequency and an approach that avoids dropping in-flight jobs.

4) Do you support preserving existing vector IDs so we can keep historical analytics consistent? If not, what's the recommended approach to maintain stable document references?

Happy to share a Pinecone export sample once we know the desired dim and a rough migration pattern.

—Sam
Sam Torres
Head of Search & Relevance, FinLine

Hi Sam — thanks for the clear questions, answered inline below. Priya / your infra folks are welcome to jump on a short tech sync tomorrow if that helps.

1) Dimensionality
- Recommendation: use 1536 for semantic embeddings by default (better out-of-the-box separation for retrieval + reranking). If cost is a concern, 768 is workable but expect slightly lower retrieval fidelity in complex queries.
- Mapping from 768 -> 1536: there is no lossless upsampling; to move to 1536 you need to re-embed the originals with a 1536 model. For hybrid approaches you can store both 768 and 1536 vectors side-by-side for A/B comparison during cutover.

2) Batching / single-GPU import
- For a 16GB GPU, practical batch sizes for import typically land between 32 and 128 depending on sequence length and model type. Start with batch_size=64 for your dry-run. Monitor GPU memory and latency; we batch asynchronously in our SDK so you can push multiple concurrent batches without blocking ingestion.

3) Auth & key rotation
- Recommended cadence: rotate ingestion keys every 30 days for production, with 2-week short-lived keys for ephemeral hosts if you can. Use a key-staging approach: provision new key, deploy to ingestion service, verify ingestion, then deprecate the old key. For in-flight jobs, the SDK supports graceful retry; configure a rolling restart window so jobs use the new key after checkpointing. We'll share the api-key-rotation-guidelines.docx with explicit steps.

4) Preserving vector IDs
- Redwood supports an external_id field on index operations; if you import with external_id set to your existing doc_id, those IDs are preserved in the index. We recommend keeping a stable external_id mapping and writing a migration log (old_id -> new_index_id) during the dry-run. That allows historical analytics to reference the stable id.

Additional notes
- Normalization: use L2 normalization on vectors before writing to the index. Keep the exact pre-processing pipeline (tokenization, lowercasing, stopword handling) identical between extraction and future re-embeds.
- Reranking: typical flow is ANN -> topK (100) -> rerank model -> return topN. We'll provide a sample reranker pipeline that works with Redwood outputs.
- Migration strategy:
   a) Export snapshot from Pinecone (vectors + metadata + external_id).
   b) Import into a staging Redwood index in parallel.
   c) Run automated parity checks (cosine similarity sampling, doc count checks, metadata integrity).
   d) Switch queries to Redwood once parity thresholds met.

If your team can drop a 5–10MB sample export (a few hundred vectors) into the shared Drive link, Rishi and I will do a quick validation and report back with a recommended batch profile and estimated import time.

Proposed next steps
- Sam: share sample export by EOD Tue
- Rishi: I'll assign an engineer session to validate the sample and produce a 30-min runbook for your infra team (target Wed afternoon)
- Marissa: I'll loop you for timeline and commercial impact if you expect a larger ingestion commit.

Thanks —
Ava
